rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Electric potential.** Potential at a point is work done per unit positive charge in bringing a test charge from infinity: V = W/q = (1/4πε₀)q/r for a point charge, measured in volts.  ·  **Potential difference.** The potential difference V₂ − V₁ equals the work done per unit charge against the field in moving between the two points; 1 V = 1 J C⁻¹.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Potential energy.** A charge q at potential V has energy U = qV; for two point charges U = q₁q₂/4πε₀r, and for a system the pairwise energies add.  ·  **Electron volt.** 1 eV is the energy gained by an electron moving through a potential difference of 1 volt: 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.  ·  **Equipotential surfaces.** These surfaces are everywhere perpendicular to field lines; no work is done moving a charge along one, and the surface of a charged conductor is equipotential.
